svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Open PowerShell and verify SSH host keys
Your Windows 10 host · Windows PowerShell
Windows PowerShell — Windows host
COMMAND / FILE CONTENT TO ENTER — PRESERVE CASE
Get-Command ssh
ssh learner@10.90.0.10
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
SSH opens the application’s Linux prompt after you verify its host fingerprint. exit returns to
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. On Windows, click Start, type PowerShell, and open Windows PowerShell as your normal user.
2. Run Get-Command ssh. If SSH is missing, open PowerShell as administrator and run Add-
WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Client~~~~0.0.1.0, then reopen normal PowerShell.
3. On each VM’s local console, run sudo ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub. Record the
public host fingerprint beside that VM’s address.
4. Back in normal PowerShell, run ssh learner@10.90.0.10. Compare the displayed fingerprint with the
application console before typing yes. Enter your learner password when asked.
5. Run hostname in the SSH session. Type exit to return to Windows. Repeat ssh learner@10.90.0.20 and
compare the CA fingerprint, then run hostname and exit.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
